--- ## title: "Converted Presentation" format: revealjs: theme: default pagetitle: 'Dynamic occupancy models' slide-number: true echo: true lang: en --- ## {content-align="center" style="font-size: 150%;"}
**Dynamic occupancy models**
::: {style='font-size: 60%;'} WILD(FISH) 8390
Inference for Models of Fish and Wildlife Population Dynamics
:::
# Overview {visibility="hidden"} ## Overview ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} When we covered static occupancy models, we focused exclusively on spatial variation.
::: {.fragment} Historically, the study of population dynamics was entirely focused on temporal variation. :::
::: {.fragment} Metapopulation models played a big role in emphasizing both spatial and temporal dynamics. :::
::: {.fragment} Dynamic occupancy models allow for inference on spatio-temporal occupancy resulting from local colonization and extinction processes. ::: ::: ## [Static (single-season) occupancy model]{style="font-size: 90%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} The model for the state process is the same as logistic regression: $$ \mathrm{logit}(\psi_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{i1} + \beta_2 x_{i2} + \cdots \\ z_i \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_i) $$ Model for the observation process conditional on the state process: $$ \mathrm{logit}(p_{ij}) = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1 x_{ij1} + \alpha_2 x_{ij2} + \cdots \\ y_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_i\times p_{ij}) $$ Definitions
::: ::: {style='font-size: 60%;'} $\psi_i$ -- probability that the species occurs at site $i$
$z_i$ -- binary presence/absence variable at site $i$
$p_{ij}$ -- probability of detecting the species at site $i$ on occasion $j$
$y_{ij}$ -- binary detection/non-detection data ::: ## Dynamic occupancy model ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Initial occupancy state (same as static model), for $k=1$. $$ z_{i,1} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_{i,1}) $$ ::: {.fragment} Occupancy state dynamics, for $k=2, \dots, K$. $$ \psi_{i,k} = z_{i,k-1}(1-\varepsilon) + (1-z_{i,k-1})\gamma \\ z_{i,k} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\psi_{i,k}) $$ ::: ::: {.fragment} Observation model $$ y_{i,j,k} \sim \mathrm{Bern}(z_{i,k}\times p) $$ ::: ::: ::: {style='font-size: 55%;'} ::: {.fragment} $\psi_{i,k}$ -- probability species occurs at site $i$ during primary period $k$
$z_{i,k}$ -- binary presence/absence variable
$\varepsilon$ -- local extinction probability
$\gamma$ -- local colonization probability
$p$ -- probability of detecting the species if it's present
$y_{i,j,k}$ -- detection data at site $i$ on secondary period $j$, primary period $k$
::: ::: ## Colonization and extinction dynamics ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} After the initial time period, the probability that a site is occupied depends on the previous state and the two probabilities: - Local colonization: $\gamma=\Pr(z_{i,k}=1|z_{i,k-1}=0)$ - Local extinction: $\varepsilon=\Pr(z_{i,k}=0|z_{i,k-1}=1)$ ::: {.fragment}
![](figure/royle_dorazio_9-1){width="20%"}
From Royle and Dorazio (2008)
::: ::: {.fragment} These probabilities can depend on spatio-temporal covariates and random effects. In spatially-explicit models, they depend on the states and distances to neighboring sites. ::: ::: ## Simulation without covariates ::: {style='font-size: 75%;'} Initial occupancy ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} nSites <- 100 nPrimary <- 10 z <- psi <- matrix(NA, nSites, nPrimary) psi[,1] <- 0.5 ## Initial occupancy prob z[,1] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi[,1]) ``` ::: Occupancy dynamics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} epsilon <- 0.3 ## Local extinction prob gamma <- 0.2 ## Local colonization prob for(k in 2:nPrimary) { psi[,k] <- z[,k-1]*(1-epsilon) + (1-z[,k-1])*gamma z[,k] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi[,k]) } ``` ::: Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} nSecondary <- 3 p <- 0.2 y <- array(NA, c(nSites, nSecondary, nPrimary)) for(i in 1:nSites) { for(k in 1:nPrimary) { y[i,,k] <- rbinom(nSecondary, size=1, prob=z[i,k]*p) } } ``` ::: ::: ## Simulated data ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%'} **Observations** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y[1:15,,1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [,1] [,2] [,3] [1,] 0 0 0 [2,] 0 0 0 [3,] 0 0 0 [4,] 1 0 0 [5,] 0 1 0 [6,] 0 0 0 [7,] 0 1 0 [8,] 0 0 0 [9,] 0 0 0 [10,] 0 0 0 [11,] 0 0 1 [12,] 0 0 0 [13,] 0 0 0 [14,] 0 0 0 [15,] 0 0 0 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%'} **Summary stats** Detections at each site
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} siteDets <- rowSums(y) # Dets at each site table(siteDets) # Frequency ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` siteDets 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 9 17 20 20 17 13 4 5 3 1 ``` ::: ::: Detections each year
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} yearDets <- apply(y, 3, sum) yearDets ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 27 30 31 28 22 15 22 27 20 21 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Prepare data in 'unmarked' Notice the new argument `numPrimary`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ## Format as nSites by (nSec*nPrimary) matrix y.wide <- matrix(y, nrow=nrow(y)) umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=y.wide, numPrimary=nPrimary) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(umf) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` unmarkedFrame Object 100 sites Maximum number of observations per site: 30 Mean number of observations per site: 30 Number of primary survey periods: 10 Number of secondary survey periods: 3 Sites with at least one detection: 83 Tabulation of y observations: 0 1 2757 243 ``` ::: ::: ## Fit the model Notice the 4 distinct formulas ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fm <- colext(~1,~1,~1,~1, umf) fm ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~1, data = umf) Initial (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -0.113 0.367 -0.309 0.758 Colonization (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -1.33 0.2 -6.66 2.7e-11 Extinction (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -0.642 0.315 -2.04 0.0417 Detection (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -1.36 0.146 -9.33 1.03e-20 AIC: 1626.912 Number of sites: 100 ``` ::: ::: ## Compare estimate to actual ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width='50%'} Estimates ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} coef(backTransform(fm, type="psi")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.4717369 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} coef(backTransform(fm, type="col")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.2092232 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} coef(backTransform(fm, type="ext")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.3447102 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} coef(backTransform(fm, type="det")) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.2042704 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width='50%'} Actual ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} psi[1,1] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} gamma ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.2 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} epsilon ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} p ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.2 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: ## Sites occupied ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} re <- ranef(fm) occupied.post <- predict(re, func=colSums, nsim=1000) plot(1:nPrimary, rowMeans(occupied.post), type="b", pch=16, xlab="Time", ylab="Sites occupied", ylim=c(0, 70)) lines(1:nPrimary, colSums(z), type="b", col=4) segments(1:nPrimary, apply(occupied.post, 1, quantile, prob=0.025), 1:nPrimary, apply(occupied.post, 1, quantile, prob=0.975)) legend(1, 70, c("Actual", "Estimated"), pch=c(1,16), col=c(4,1), lty=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-dynamic-occupancy_files/figure-revealjs/re-1.png){fig-align='center' width=60%} ::: ::: ::: ## The JAGS model [dynocc-model.jag](dynocc-model.jag) ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { psi1 ~ dunif(0, 1) ## initial occupancy epsilon ~ dunif(0, 1) ## local extinction gamma ~ dunif(0, 1) ## local colonization p ~ dunif(0, 1) ## detection prob for(i in 1:nSites) { psi[i,1] <- psi1 z[i,1] ~ dbern(psi[i,1]) for(k in 2:K) { psi[i,k] <- z[i,k-1]*(1-epsilon) + (1-z[i,k-1])*gamma z[i,k] ~ dbern(psi[i,k]) } for(k in 1:K) { for(j in 1:J) { y[i,j,k] ~ dbern(z[i,k]*p) } } } for(k in 1:K) { N[k] <- sum(z[,k]) ## Sites occupied } } ``` ::: ::: ## Data, inits, and parameters Put data in a named list ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.data <- list(y=y, nSites=nSites, J=nSecondary, K=nPrimary) ``` ::: Initial values ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.inits <- function() { list(psi1=runif(1), epsilon=runif(1), gamma=runif(1), p=runif(1), z=matrix(1, nSites, nPrimary)) } ``` ::: Parameters to monitor ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.pars <- c("psi1", "epsilon", "gamma", "p", "N") ``` ::: ## MCMC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(jagsUI) jags.post.samples <- jags.basic(data=jags.data, inits=jags.inits, parameters.to.save=jags.pars, model.file="dynocc-model.jag", n.chains=3, n.adapt=100, n.burnin=0, n.iter=2000, parallel=TRUE) ``` ::: ## Summarize output ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(jags.post.samples[,jags.pars[1:4]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Iterations = 101:2100 Thinning interval = 1 Number of chains = 3 Sample size per chain = 2000 1. Empirical mean and standard deviation for each variable, plus standard error of the mean: Mean SD Naive SE Time-series SE psi1 0.4837 0.08828 0.0011397 0.003077 epsilon 0.3526 0.06522 0.0008420 0.004007 gamma 0.2158 0.03444 0.0004446 0.001586 p 0.2041 0.02326 0.0003003 0.001325 2. Quantiles for each variable: 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% psi1 0.3216 0.4204 0.4808 0.5419 0.6648 epsilon 0.2310 0.3062 0.3518 0.3977 0.4836 gamma 0.1550 0.1922 0.2143 0.2372 0.2893 p 0.1617 0.1877 0.2030 0.2196 0.2515 ``` ::: ::: ## Traceplots and density plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(jags.post.samples[,jags.pars[1:4]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-dynamic-occupancy_files/figure-revealjs/bugs-plot1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=80%} ::: ::: ## [Dynamic occupancy models with covariates]{style="font-size: 80%;"} ::: {style='font-size: 65%;'} Three types of covariates: 1. Site covariates - These vary among sites, but not among occasions - Can be used to model $\psi_1$, $\varepsilon$, $\gamma$, and $p$ - Called `siteCovs` in 'unmarked' ::: {.fragment} 2. Primary sampling period covariates - These vary among sites and among, but not within, primary periods - Can be used to model $\varepsilon$, $\gamma$, and $p$ - Called `yearlySiteCovs` in 'unmarked' ::: ::: {.fragment} 3. Secondary sampling period covariates - These vary among sites and among and within primary periods - Can be used to model $p$ - Called `obsCovs` in 'unmarked' ::: ::: ## Simulation with covariates ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} Initial occupancy ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} beta0.psi <- -1; beta1.psi <- 1 elevation <- rnorm(nSites) ## site covariate z2 <- psi2 <- matrix(NA, nSites, nPrimary) psi2[,1] <- plogis(beta0.psi + beta1.psi*elevation) z2[,1] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi2[,1]) ``` ::: Occupancy dynamics ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} epsilon2 <- 0.3 ## Local extinction prob temperature <- matrix(rnorm(nSites*nPrimary)*elevation, ## Primary period covariate nrow=nSites) beta0.gamma <- -2; beta1.gamma <- -1 gamma2 <- plogis(beta0.gamma + beta1.gamma*temperature) for(k in 2:nPrimary) { psi2[,k] <- z2[,k-1]*(1-epsilon2) + (1-z2[,k-1])*gamma2[,k-1] z2[,k] <- rbinom(n=nSites, size=1, prob=psi2[,k]) } ``` ::: Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p2 <- 0.2 y2 <- array(NA, c(nSites, nSecondary, nPrimary)) for(i in 1:nSites) { for(k in 1:nPrimary) { y2[i,,k] <- rbinom(nSecondary, size=1, prob=z2[i,k]*p2) } } ``` ::: ::: ## Prepare data in 'unmarked' ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Notice the new arguments `numPrimary` and `yearlySiteCovs`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y2.wide <- matrix(y2, nrow=nrow(y2)) ## nSites by (nSec*nPrimary) matrix umf2 <- unmarkedMultFrame(y=y2.wide, numPrimary=nPrimary, siteCovs=data.frame(elevation), yearlySiteCovs=list(temp=temperature)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(umf2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` unmarkedFrame Object 100 sites Maximum number of observations per site: 30 Mean number of observations per site: 30 Number of primary survey periods: 10 Number of secondary survey periods: 3 Sites with at least one detection: 70 Tabulation of y observations: 0 1 2798 202 Site-level covariates: elevation Min. :-2.8755 1st Qu.:-0.7162 Median :-0.1279 Mean :-0.1097 3rd Qu.: 0.5059 Max. : 2.1723 Yearly-site-level covariates: temp Min. :-5.260423 1st Qu.:-0.335854 Median :-0.004001 Mean :-0.015024 3rd Qu.: 0.314745 Max. : 7.827805 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Fit the model ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Notice the 4 distinct formulas ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fm2 <- colext(~elevation,~temp,~1,~1, umf2) fm2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: colext(psiformula = ~elevation, gammaformula = ~temp, epsilonformula = ~1, pformula = ~1, data = umf2) Initial (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) (Intercept) -1.99 0.449 -4.43 9.27e-06 elevation 1.04 0.500 2.09 3.70e-02 Colonization (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) (Intercept) -1.90 0.185 -10.24 1.34e-24 temp -0.72 0.209 -3.44 5.88e-04 Extinction (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -0.977 0.314 -3.11 0.00188 Detection (logit-scale): Estimate SE z P(>|z|) -1.25 0.139 -9.02 1.81e-19 AIC: 1351.396 Number of sites: 100 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Prediction in unmarked Create data frame with prediction covariates. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pred.data <- data.frame(temp=seq(from=-5, to=4, length=50)) ``` ::: Get predictions of $\gamma$ for each row of prediction data. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gamma.pred <- predict(fm2, newdata=pred.data, type='col', append=TRUE) ``` ::: ## Prediction in unmarked ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(Predicted ~ temp, gamma.pred, type="l", ylab="Colonization probability", xlab="Standardized temperature", ylim=0:1, lwd=2) lines(lower ~ temp, gamma.pred, col=gray(0.6)) lines(upper ~ temp, gamma.pred, col=gray(0.6)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-dynamic-occupancy_files/figure-revealjs/pred-gamma1-1.png){fig-align='center' width=60%} ::: ::: ::: ## The JAGS model [dynocc-model-covars.jag](dynocc-model-covars.jag) ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` model { beta0.psi ~ dnorm(0, 0.5) ## Intercept of initial occupancy beta1.psi ~ dnorm(0, 0.5) ## Effect of elevation epsilon ~ dunif(0, 1) ## Local extinction beta0.gamma ~ dnorm(0, 0.5) ## Intercept of colonization beta1.gamma ~ dnorm(0, 0.5) ## Effect of temperature p ~ dunif(0, 1) ## detection prob for(i in 1:nSites) { logit(psi[i,1]) <- beta0.psi + beta1.psi*elevation[i] z[i,1] ~ dbern(psi[i,1]) for(k in 2:K) { logit(gamma[i,k-1]) <- beta0.gamma + beta1.gamma*temp[i,k-1] psi[i,k] <- z[i,k-1]*(1-epsilon) + (1-z[i,k-1])*gamma[i,k-1] z[i,k] ~ dbern(psi[i,k]) } for(k in 1:K) { for(j in 1:J) { y[i,j,k] ~ dbern(z[i,k]*p) } } } for(k in 1:K) { N[k] <- sum(z[,k]) ## Sites occupied } } ``` ::: ::: ## Data, inits, and parameters Put data in a named list ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.data.covs <- list(y=y2, nSites=nSites, elevation=elevation, temp=temperature, J=nSecondary, K=nPrimary) ``` ::: Initial values ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.inits.covs <- function() { list(beta0.psi=rnorm(1), beta1.psi=rnorm(1), epsilon=runif(1), beta0.gamma=rnorm(1), beta1.gamma=rnorm(1), p=runif(1), z=matrix(1, nSites, nPrimary)) } ``` ::: Parameters to monitor ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} jags.pars.covs <- c("beta0.psi", "beta1.psi", "epsilon", "beta0.gamma", "beta1.gamma", "p", "N") ``` ::: ## MCMC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(jagsUI) jags.post.samples.covs <- jags.basic( data=jags.data.covs, inits=jags.inits.covs, parameters.to.save=jags.pars.covs, model.file="dynocc-model-covars.jag", n.chains=3, n.adapt=100, n.burnin=0, n.iter=2000, parallel=TRUE) ``` ::: ## Summarize output ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} summary(jags.post.samples.covs[,jags.pars.covs[1:6]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Iterations = 101:2100 Thinning interval = 1 Number of chains = 3 Sample size per chain = 2000 1. Empirical mean and standard deviation for each variable, plus standard error of the mean: Mean SD Naive SE Time-series SE beta0.psi -1.8528 0.40464 0.0052239 0.013782 beta1.psi 0.9290 0.44821 0.0057864 0.015942 epsilon 0.2801 0.06036 0.0007792 0.003408 beta0.gamma -1.8652 0.18462 0.0023835 0.006602 beta1.gamma -0.7330 0.21694 0.0028007 0.008412 p 0.2203 0.02360 0.0003046 0.001141 2. Quantiles for each variable: 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% beta0.psi -2.7135 -2.1099 -1.8352 -1.5730 -1.1064 beta1.psi 0.1114 0.6198 0.9011 1.2152 1.8717 epsilon 0.1726 0.2386 0.2767 0.3183 0.4073 beta0.gamma -2.2364 -1.9851 -1.8630 -1.7397 -1.5165 beta1.gamma -1.2117 -0.8657 -0.7172 -0.5853 -0.3558 p 0.1780 0.2037 0.2195 0.2355 0.2690 ``` ::: ::: ## Traceplots and density plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(jags.post.samples.covs[,jags.pars.covs[1:3]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-dynamic-occupancy_files/figure-revealjs/bugs-plot1-cov-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: ## Traceplots and density plots ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(jags.post.samples.covs[,jags.pars.covs[4:6]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-dynamic-occupancy_files/figure-revealjs/bugs-plot2-cov-1.png){fig-align='center' width=70%} ::: ::: ## Sites occupied Extract posterior samples of $N_t$ and compute summary stats. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(coda) N.names <- grep("N\\[", varnames(jags.post.samples.covs) ) N.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.samples.covs[,N.names]) N.post.mean <- colMeans(N.post) N.post.lower <- apply(N.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.025) N.post.upper <- apply(N.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.975) ``` ::: ## Sites occupied ::: {style='font-size: 70%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} plot(1:nPrimary, N.post.mean, type="b", ylim=c(0, 70), pch=16, xlab="Time", ylab="Sites occupied") segments(1:nPrimary, N.post.lower, 1:nPrimary, N.post.upper) lines(1:nPrimary, colSums(z2), type="b", col=4) legend(1, 70, c("Actual", "Estimated"), pch=c(1,16), col=c(4,1), lty=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-dynamic-occupancy_files/figure-revealjs/N-post-covs-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=65%} ::: ::: ::: ## Temperature and colonization ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Extract posterior samples of colonization coefficients, and then predict $\gamma$ for each posterior draw.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} beta.post <- as.matrix(jags.post.samples.covs[,c( "beta0.gamma","beta1.gamma")]) temperature.seq <- seq(-5, 5, length=50) n.samples <- nrow(beta.post) gamma.post <- matrix(NA, n.samples, length(temperature.seq)) for(i in 1:n.samples) { gamma.post[i,] <- plogis(beta.post[i,1] + beta.post[i,2]*temperature.seq) } gamma.post.mean <- colMeans(gamma.post) gamma.post.lower <- apply(gamma.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.025) gamma.post.upper <- apply(gamma.post, 2, quantile, prob=0.975) ``` ::: ::: ## Temperature and colonization ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true"} matplot(temperature.seq, t(gamma.post[seq(1,n.samples,10),]), type="l", xlab="Temperature (standardized)", ylab="Colonization prob", col=gray(0.9)) lines(temperature.seq, gamma.post.mean, lwd=3, col="blue") lines(temperature.seq, gamma.post.lower, col="blue") lines(temperature.seq, gamma.post.upper, col="blue") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](lecture-dynamic-occupancy_files/figure-revealjs/gamma-post-covs-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=65%} ::: ::: ::: ## Concluding thoughts ::: {style='font-size: 80%;'} Although we didn't demonstrate, these models are great for creating dynamic species distribution maps.
::: {.fragment} The spatially-explicit versions are also great for modeling metapopulation dynamics and viability. :::
::: {.fragment} Most of the assumptions that we covered for the static models apply, except that we've relaxed the closure assumption. :::
::: {.fragment} Check out the new R package [spOccupancy](https://www.jeffdoser.com/files/spoccupancy-web/) for a wide range of Bayesian occupancy models. ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
